psi_bound.assumptions: lambda = 0 assumed, and orbit inclined in the same direction as the stellar spin axis (Sect. 5.1)
psi_bound.implication: psi >= ~71 deg rules out a well-aligned orbit. Because the planet transits (i near 90 deg) and i* is only ~18 deg, cos(psi) is approximately sin(i*)cos(lambda), so psi stays within roughly 90 +/- i* whatever lambda is, i.e. near-polar. caveats: A planet's sky-plane orbital inclination was never used as an obliquity. The Bowler+2023 Delta i values are |i* - i_o| minimum obliquities that the paper itself computes, not our arithmetic.

Classification rule: angle = psi if known, else |lambda| (lambda folded into 0-180, e.g. GJ 3090 b lambda = 208 -> 152); prograde < 70, polar 70-110, retrograde > 110. Where only a lower bound exists whose 95% interval reaches 0, the class is 'unclear'.

TRAPPIST-1: Brady+2023's preferred model fits ONE obliquity for b-g (coplanar assumption). It is recorded under each planet with shared_system_value=true; the per-planet fits are in other_measurements. TRAPPIST-1 h was not observed.
TEPCat still lists the arXiv-v1 numbers for GJ 3470 b (lambda 101, psi 97); the refereed paper gives lambda 98 +15/-12, psi 95 +9/-8.
TEPCat stores GJ 523 b as psi = 90 +28.6/-0; the paper gives only psi >= 71.4 +4.7/-5.0 under lambda = 0.
GJ 9827 values come from the A&A abstract (full text blocked by a 403), cross-checked against TEPCat and the NASA Exoplanet Archive; the table/section number was not seen directly.

Earth's 7.155 deg (Beck & Giles 2005) could not be re-read (ADS captcha, no arXiv copy). The other seven Solar System values are not printed values: they were recomputed here from JPL J2000 elements and the IAU solar pole, and agree with the cells to 0.01 deg.

Bibcodes for 2026 papers: Carteret+ (A&A 713, L15) and Lin+ (ApJL 1005, L25) follow the ADS pattern from the journal reference (Lin's taken from TEPCat).
